verdict.rationale: Angular's own docs claim it builds fast applications that scale with team size. They point to Signals for fine-grained reactivity, components plus dependency injection for modular organization, a style guide, and CLI tooling for updates, linting and caching. Community reports add that performance is great with AOT and tree-shaking, and a Google engineer says >100k SLOC internal apps stay maintainable when teams follow the style guide. The digest-cycle scaling complaints describe legacy AngularJS dirty-checking, so they do not concretely contradict modern Angular. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party performance guidance (e.g., lazy loading, change-detection tuning, bundle budgets), independent hands-on evidence of modern Angular at large scale, and documentation beyond marketing taglines.
